runners_data.comment: Hello Garda was third when last seen just five days ago and already has experience over today's distance, form that stamps him a threat to the selection on a rating of 66; the yard's form (0 of 23 in the last fortnight) is the concern.

runners_data.comment: Keep Under Wraps refused on his most recent outing and is fresh again 33 days on, leaving little worthwhile form to judge him by; he remains unexposed and open to improvement if fortune favours him this time.

runners_data.name: Nicolai

runners_data.comment: Nicolai is unraced, with 108 days since his last entry, leaving nothing on the book to judge him by; he remains open to improvement on his first real test.

runners_data.name: Salkadan

runners_data.comment: Salkadan is unraced and has had 52 days since his last entry, though the stable is in good order, landing 10 of its last 35 in the past fortnight; he remains open to improvement once given the chance to show it.

runners_data.name: Us Officer

runners_data.name: Zooter

runners_data.comment: Zooter is unraced, with 31 days since his last entry, leaving no form to judge him on; he remains open to improvement once he gets the chance to show it.

runners_data.name: Adba
runners_data.note: Harry Kimber partners a horse that has finished no better than fifth in five hurdles runs; the layoff of 91 days and uninspiring form string on a mix of Soft and Standard make it hard to see where the improvement comes from, and being pushed out of its natural rear position further reduces its chance in this specific shape.
runners_data.comment: Adba is unraced, with 91 days since her last entry, leaving nothing on the book to judge her by; she remains open to improvement on her first real test.

races.paceDynamic: Us Officer is the sole confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the lead from a hold-up profile, and is likely to set a steady, uncontested gallop around Uttoxeter's turning 2m on Good ground — a surface that rewards economical travellers rather than grinders. Behind him, Salkadan, Nicolai, Hello Garda and Adba are all genuine hold-up types compressed into midfield on the map because the field is stacked with closers; in practice, most will race in a tight, shuffled bunch behind a moderate pace. This configuration — one reluctant front-runner setting a sustainable tempo with the pack bunched — creates a falsely run race where position and jump quality matter more than stamina. The race shape strongly favours horses who can travel close to the pace without being on the bridle early, quicken from a handy position over the final two hurdles, and have the tactical sharpness to exploit a slow-burn tempo; true hold-up horses that must make up ground late will find little real estate to work with. The field holds more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear — Salkadan (Harry Skelton, Dan Skelton), Nicolai, and Hello Garda are most likely to drift closest to a prominent berth given the compressed midfield, while others such as Adba and Al Za'ama face the toughest redistribution challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Handy Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Us Officer sets a modest uncontested gallop and the bunch arrives at the last flight in a heap, horses racing closest to the pace with a clean jump win.
scenarios.body: Us Officer controls a false pace and the race becomes a sprint from the second-last, rewarding any horse who has travelled smoothly in his slipstream without being buried in traffic; Salkadan and Zooter have the form and tactical versatility to pounce from close range.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sticks On
scenarios.trigger: If Us Officer, racing out of his natural role but uncontested on the lead, sets a rhythm that suits him and jumps well enough to maintain his advantage into the straight.
scenarios.body: A modest pace that he himself controls can paradoxically suit Us Officer if the hold-up pack behind him fails to organise quickly enough after the last; the lone galloper who dictates every fraction and jumps cleanly has a meaningful advantage in a field of inexperienced hurdlers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply from halfway and creates genuine early pressure, burning out the leaders and leaving a late run viable for true hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Vietnorm has already demonstrated strong finishing ability on Good ground and won over 16f on Good, giving him the stamina and turn-of-foot profile to pick off tired rivals in the closing stages; however, the scenario depends on pace that may simply not materialise, making this reliant on race evolution beyond what the set-up suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos At Last Flight
scenarios.trigger: If there is a significant jumping incident or multiple fallers/errors at the final hurdle that reshuffles the order dramatically.
scenarios.body: In a field of novice juveniles with limited hurdles experience, a calamity at the last is a genuine low-probability but non-trivial event; whoever jumps cleanly and is not impeded takes advantage regardless of running style.

watchPoints.text: Us Officer is racing out of his natural hold-up role on the lead — watch whether Brendan Powell settles him or whether the horse fights for his head early, because a ragged gallop from the pace-setter will scramble the entire race shape.

Nicolai, Hello Garda and Al Za'ama are all true hold-up types compressed into midfield; watch for a traffic-jam scenario on the final bend where multiple horses attempt to find a run simultaneously and interference becomes a real danger.

Keep Under Wraps has an 'R' in his form string and is lightly raced — watch for any early signs of reluctance or jumping anxiety from Jack Tudor's mount, as a refusal or blunder could cause chaos in the pack behind.

Salkadan is 52 days fresh for the powerful Dan Skelton and Harry Skelton combination with a 10/35 trainer 14-day record — watch for market moves on this one as Skelton juveniles arriving fresh in this type of race often show improved form.

Good ground is confirmed for all races at Uttoxeter today — watch for any horses that are reported by connections or show in pre-race work to have a preference for cut in the ground, as Al Za'ama and Nicolai both have limited Good-ground form compared to rivals.

races.paceDynamic: No Risk Today is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, she will dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front on Good ground at Uttoxeter — a track that suits front-running types over 2m hurdles. The pace will be sustainable rather than scorching, meaning the race is unlikely to fall apart into a sprint finish but also unlikely to be so slow that hold-up horses can simply pounce from nowhere. Culligran is the only horse with a Prominent tag and will sit closest to No Risk Today, giving the front two a small buffer over the rest. This shape overwhelmingly favours prominent and front-running profiles — horses who can track the pace comfortably and strike from a winning position turning in — while the true hold-up types face a significant challenge manufacturing their finishing effort when the early gallop is controlled rather than searching. This field contains far more hold-up types than the race map can place at the rear in their natural position; Curious Mrs Fox, Dotties Promise, Northern Rose, Jukebox Annie, Myfavouritesister and Granny B are all genuine come-from-behind horses but are mapped to midfield because the sheer volume of H-style runners compresses the field — No Risk Today and Culligran are the most likely to actually secure their natural positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If No Risk Today bowls along uncontested and sets a genuine but controlled pace that the hold-up pack cannot overhaul.
scenarios.body: No Risk Today dictates every yard at a rhythm that suits her, and any challengers must work hard to reel her in from a prominent position rather than a late swoop; Culligran, tracking in second, is ideally placed to pounce if the leader weakens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is just strong enough to stretch hold-up horses but leave Culligran and any prominent tracker poised for a decisive move at the second-last.
scenarios.body: Culligran or Prettylady, sitting within a length or two of the pace throughout, moves smoothly into contention jumping the final hurdle and out-stays a tiring No Risk Today; their ability to race close to the gallop without expending energy hunting down the leader is the decisive edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Arrives
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough to burn off the prominent types and create a truly-run race where a late finisher can make up ground.
scenarios.body: Lady Fortune or Northern Rose, both of whom have shown the ability to produce a sustained late run on Good ground, manage to thread through the compressed midfield and catch a flat-to-the-boards front pair; the shape must collapse on the leaders for this to materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Muddling Finish
scenarios.trigger: If No Risk Today crawls early and the field concertinas, turning the race into a messy sprint from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A bunched, sprint-like finish from the last hurdle benefits the freshest legs and best jumper in the pack; Prettylady, a young mare in good form on Good ground, and Lady Fortune, who has won at this trip, are both athletic enough to quicken sharply in a stolen-march scenario.

watchPoints.text: No Risk Today's gallop tempo is the key variable — if Jack Hogan allows her to bowl along at a true pace, the race is set for a front-runners' benefit, but any hesitation early could compress the field and open the race up.

Culligran is the one horse guaranteed a perfect stalking position directly behind the leader — if No Risk Today weakens from the second-last, Kielan Woods will be first to capitalise and this horse's Good-ground place record makes her the primary danger.
The volume of redistributed hold-up horses (six runners) means the midfield will be congested — watch for traffic issues and interference from the home turn as multiple jockeys hunt the same gap.

Prettylady's yard (Oliver Greenall & Josh Guerriero, T14: 2/8) is in active form and Jack Tudor is a reliable pilot for a progressive mare — monitor her position jumping the final hurdle as she may sit closer than her H-tag suggests.

Lady Fortune is only 11 days off her last run, which may mean she is fit and cherry-ripe or alternatively returning before fully wound down — watch for any signs of freshness or flat-footedness early under the 5lb claimer Isabelle Ryder.

races.paceDynamic: Bright Legend is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to contest the lead from the gates, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested gallop on Good ground over 2m at Uttoxeter. The pace will be honest but controlled — Bright Legend dictating a rhythm that is unlikely to be pressured into something unsustainable, meaning the race will not truly string out until the turn for home. This field contains more prominent and prominent-leaning types than the shape can accommodate: Emerald Time, Diesel Line, and King Sacre are all natural pace horses or prominent movers who have been pushed back into midfield on the map precisely because there is insufficient room at the front, and Drombeg Lad and Romany Brown will be competing for the seats directly behind Bright Legend. Of those, Drombeg Lad — with a six-from-six record on Good and fresh form — and Romany Brown are likeliest to secure those prominent berths, while Emerald Time, Diesel Line, and King Sacre will be forced to race out of their preferred roles. A controlled, single-pace gallop from an uncontested front-runner on Good turf favours horses racing prominently in their natural position, with the tactical premium going to those who can sit close to the pace without burning energy and produce a jump-for-jump finish from the second-last.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bright Legend Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bright Legend leads throughout at a sustainable tempo and the race becomes a test of jumping accuracy and staying power from the front.
scenarios.body: Bright Legend sets a measured gallop with no rival able or willing to press, turning the race into a war of attrition over the final two flights where clean jumping and fitness from 89 days off become decisive; horses racing genuinely prominent — Drombeg Lad and Romany Brown — are ideally placed to pounce if Bright Legend tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Bright Legend's 89-day absence tells late and the genuinely prominent Drombeg Lad or Romany Brown pick him off from the second-last flight.
scenarios.body: The controlled tempo suits horses travelling comfortably just off the pace, and a leader who has not raced in nearly three months may lack the race-sharpness to hold on; Drombeg Lad's six-from-six Good-going record and Romany Brown's proven class at the trip make them the most dangerous challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a closing run, allowing Ice Jet or War Correspondent to pick up from off the pace in the straight.
scenarios.body: Ice Jet's recent form is outstanding — three consecutive wins over 20f — and Harry Skelton will be hunting cover before unleashing a late challenge; however, the probability is tempered by the likelihood that Bright Legend's unchallenged lead produces a pace too moderate to create the gap hold-up horses need.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scenario — Front Blows Up
scenarios.trigger: If Bright Legend bowls along at a pace beyond his fitness level post-layoff and the field fragments, creating a cavalry charge finish from the second-last.
scenarios.body: A genuinely stop-start or collapse-at-the-death shape would release all the crowded prominent types simultaneously, but this requires Bright Legend to badly misjudge his own pace — unlikely given the moderate-field dynamic and Good ground; Emerald Time or Diesel Line, both natural pace horses racing out of role in midfield, would be the unexpected beneficiaries if forced wider gaps emerge.

watchPoints.text: Watch Bright Legend's jumping from the first flight — any mistake early could disrupt what should be a clean, uncontested lead and completely alter the race shape, gifting a tactical advantage to Drombeg Lad and Romany Brown immediately behind.|

Ice Jet ran just two days ago; watch whether Harry Skelton sits quietly and conserves energy rather than committing early, as signs of a quick-fire turnaround fatigue could surface in the final 3 flights.|

Monitor how aggressively Emerald Time, Diesel Line, and King Sacre are ridden out of the gates — if two or more of these displaced prominent types push forward regardless, the pace will spike and the race shape changes dramatically, benefiting true hold-up horses.|

Drombeg Lad's six-from-six Good-going record is worth tracking in-running; if he sits smoothly in second or third throughout and jumps the second-last cleanly, his chance of landing a blow is materially stronger than his OR of 108 alone would suggest.|

races.paceDynamic: Sony Bill is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with Harry Cobden in the saddle, will dictate from the outset on Good ground over this 3m trip at Uttoxeter — a track that rewards horses who travel well in front without being harried. The prominent pack is badly congested: Sure Touch, Grand Clermont, Sunray Shadow, and Imperial Alex all want to race in the first three or four, meaning there will be a natural shuffle for position in the early stages that could inject more pressure on Sony Bill than his form alone might suggest. Between the 2nd-last and last there is genuine traffic danger as this group of prominent types, some of whom have been redistributed on the map, converge in a tight bunch. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all occupy their natural position — Hold Your Fort, Stans The Man, and The Flying Poet are true prominent racers who are most likely to find themselves further back than they'd prefer, with Sony Bill and Sunray Shadow best placed to actually secure their natural positions given connections and recent form. This race shape most favours a strong-travelling prominent horse who is comfortable racing just off the pace and possesses the jumping accuracy to pick off rivals approaching the last two fences — Sunray Shadow's profile fits that bill most cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Sony Bill (Harry Cobden) must be watched at every fence — as the lone confirmed pace-setter, any jumping error or loss of rhythm from him would immediately alter the entire race shape and trigger an unplanned early scramble for the lead.

The congestion of prominent types (Sure Touch, Grand Clermont, Sunray Shadow, Imperial Alex) creates a genuine collision risk 2-3 out as they converge on a tight Uttoxeter bend — watch for bumping or interference that could cost any of these horses momentum at the critical stage.

Bagheera Ginge (Sam Twiston-Davies) must be tracked from 4 out — if she is buried in traffic because the prominent battle fragments the field, Twiston-Davies will need a clear run that may not materialise until the last fence.

Hold Your Fort and Stans The Man, both redistributed prominent types racing out of role, are worth monitoring in the early stages for signs of restlessness or overcrowding — either could disrupt rivals if they attempt to push forward from a mid-field position.

Sunray Shadow's tp (tongue-tie and cheekpieces) headgear means she needs to be measured at the start — if she jumps off sharply and gets into a battle for position with Sony Bill rather than sitting just behind, it could compromise the relaxed prominent role that suits her best.

races.paceDynamic: Idaho Fire is the sole confirmed front-runner and, critically, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — this horse should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off over 2m7½f on Good ground. Behind the leader, Zillow, Shallow River, Karnaval Point, and Paddy De Pole all want prominent positions, creating a congested pocket of four horses jostling for the two or three berths available in the first half-mile, with real collision risk between the second fence and the third-last flight. This field contains more prominent-natured horses than the race shape can accommodate: Pike Road and Divilabother are genuine front-running or prominent types who are likely to find themselves racing out of their natural position, dropping into midfield through no tactical preference of their own. With Idaho Fire controlling an honest but uncontested pace, the tactical verdict is clear — horses who can race prominently without burning fuel in the early scramble, and who possess the stamina to sustain a balanced gallop over this extended trip on a sound surface, are best placed; specifically, prominent runners with proven Good-ground form at this sort of trip will be favoured over the redistributed midfielders who cannot exploit their natural style.

scenarios.title: Idaho Fire Controls, Prominent Wins

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion in the first half-mile — Zillow, Shallow River, Karnaval Point, and Paddy De Pole all want the same handful of positions; watch for bumping, checked runs, or horses being shuffled back entering the back straight.

Divilabother ran just two days ago — monitor any signs of fatigue or distress in the paddock and early in the race; a horse racing on quick back-to-back days over an extended trip on Good ground is a notable welfare and form concern.

Pike Road is being forced to race out of his natural prominent position due to field congestion — watch whether Freddie Keighley (5) attempts to push forward and collide with the established prominent group, which could unsettle multiple horses at a crucial stage.

Idaho Fire's stamina at 2m7½f is unproven — if the front-runner begins to shorten stride markedly before the second-last, the race could open up suddenly for hold-up types like Tyson or Roger Pol who have banked their energy.

Roger Pol's apprentice rider Isabelle Ryder (5lb) has solid recent form for Jamie Snowden but will face a significant positional challenge managing a hold-up horse in a field with this much early traffic — watch whether she can find a clean passage on the outside from the third-last onwards.

races.paceDynamic: Belle Le Grand is the confirmed lone front-runner and will dictate from the front without any genuine pressure, setting a measured, sustainable gallop over 2m4f on Good ground at Uttoxeter. Ras Kassar and At The Oche are the nearest threats positionally as prominent types but neither is a natural pace-presser, meaning Belle Le Grand can control tempo and conserve energy through the middle stages. The redistributed hold-up horses — Lakefield Flyer, Hudson, and A Dublin Job — are true closers forced into a midfield map position because the rear of the field is overcrowded with hold-up types, so their actual finishing positions will be further back than the map implies. This race shape — a lone, uncontested front-runner on a fair gallop — strongly favours prominent-to-mid-pack trackers who can stalk the pace and produce a sustained jump at the second-last, with hold-up horses at a disadvantage given the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to produce a truly end-to-end test that stretches the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Trackers Strike

scenarios.trigger: If early fencing errors, a fall, or an unexpected pace injection disrupts the settled tempo and scrambles positions.
scenarios.body: Buddah Castle's recent unseating record and the presence of a field with several shape mismatches creates tactical disorder that could suit a versatile, adaptable type; At The Oche's consistency from any position gives it resilience in a messy scenario.

watchPoints.text: Buddah Castle has unseated in two straight races — watch his jumping at every fence; a jumping blunder or another unseating could cause serious interference for horses tracking close behind.

Belle Le Grand's stamina over 2m4f is unproven — if she weakens abruptly from the second-last fence, horses immediately tracking her (Ras Kassar, At The Oche) must navigate around a tiring leader, potentially hindering their own finishes.

Ras Kassar's Going suitability is a live concern — almost all his form reads on Heavy or Heavier surfaces; if he struggles to go the early pace on Good ground, he could drop out suddenly and impede the genuine hold-up horses trying to weave through.

The three redistributed hold-up horses (Lakefield Flyer, Hudson, A Dublin Job) will all be racing out of their natural position — watch for congestion in the rear-midfield area through the first circuit as they jostle for space they would normally have to themselves.

At The Oche's 125-day absence makes his first-fence jumping worth monitoring; if he is rusty early, his prominent position could become costly, but if he settles cleanly he is ideally placed for the expected race shape.

runners_data.comment: An eighth last time out extends a run without a top-three finish in its last four, and a 93-day absence raises fitness questions; Crafty Gael has run over today's trip and going before and rates a workable 102 if sharp fresh.

runners_data.name: Luminaries
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with headgear (tp) who has shown ability with 3 wins in similar conditions historically, but recent form of P99-07 is worrying and Sean Quinlan will need to find early cover; the prominent style at least means he can sit handy behind Iamyouare and avoid the need for a strong pace.
runners_data.comment: A run of finishes no better than seventh in its last five starts, including two ninths and a pulled up, leaves Luminaries hard to fancy at the foot of these figures on 91, though this gelding has at least run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Warner's Cross
runners_data.note: Has placed five times in comparable conditions but carries the highest going concern flag (hg:h) and has not run for 76 days; a genuine hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to field congestion, Harry Reed is a less experienced rider who may find it harder to manufacture the ideal position.
runners_data.comment: Two pulled-up efforts sandwiched between modest fifths and a sixth in its last five starts, plus a 76-day layoff, make Warner's Cross hard to fancy on our figures at 99, though it has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Illico De Montave
runners_data.note: Has not run for 329 days — an enormous absence — and has never won or placed across 11 comparable efforts; Ben Poste on board and a natural hold-up style that is squeezed into midfield in this shape makes his chance negligible without a career-best performance on reappearance.
runners_data.comment: Well below form with finishes no better than seventh in its last four starts, and out of action for 329 days, Illico De Montave is hard to fancy at 97 on our figures, though it has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Iamyouare is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 2m4f handicap hurdle and should lead from the outset under Theo Gillard, setting a sustainable, uncontested gallop on good ground that is unlikely to be pressured from the front. Pure Logic and Luminaries are the only other horses with prominent inclinations, meaning the pace is unlikely to be fierce — Iamyouare can control tempo, conserve energy, and potentially steal a meaningful advantage into the straight. This shape — a lone leader dictating a measured gallop over an extended trip — classically favours horses who can travel prominently or make smooth headway from midfield, rather than pure deep closers who need a strong pace to reel in. Beny Nahar Road, Crafty Gael, Warner's Cross, and Illico De Montave are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield map because the field's true rear contingent is too large to place honestly at the back — of those, Crafty Gael (Sean Bowen) and Jafimgoso (Harry Skelton) are the ones most likely to find a workable position given their riders' tactical awareness.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Iamyouare Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Iamyouare leads at a steady, uncontested gallop and the field settles tamely behind, preserving his energy for the run-in.
scenarios.body: Iamyouare dictates every fraction on good ground over a trip he has won over before, and without a challenger to force him wide or quicken him up, he can find his own rhythm and hold on gamely; this shape rewards the horse on the lead and those who tracked closest, notably Pure Logic and Luminaries who can stay within striking range throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Iamyouare sets a modest pace that allows the prominent trackers to sit just off his shoulder and quicken past him in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Pure Logic and Luminaries both have the headgear (tp) to race keenly into a lead vacancy and, with a gentle gallop, they can travel comfortably before asserting from the second-last; Jafimgoso, a proven good-ground winner ridden by Harry Skelton, has the class (OR 101, 2W in similar going) to pick these off with a well-timed challenge from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race due to prominent runners injecting tempo, creating genuine end-to-end gallop that suits those off the pace.
scenarios.body: Royal Rocket (Harry Cobden) and Jafimgoso both have proven ability to finish strongly on good ground, and a genuinely run race over 2m4f would play to their stamina and class; however, true hold-up horses like Beny Nahar Road and Crafty Gael are unlikely to benefit fully as they will have been forced forward from their natural position rather than timing a late run from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers, pull-ups, or a catastrophic error from Iamyouare scrambles the race shape entirely, leaving no coherent pace scenario.
scenarios.body: In a field with OR ratings spanning 105 down to 71 and several horses with modest recent form strings (Crafty Gael 008, Illico De Montave 70/07), a messy race could open the door to a rank outsider benefiting from fortune; Purple Owl, placed twice on good ground, has the profile to capitalise if a vacancy opens up mid-race.

watchPoints.text: Iamyouare's pace control is critical — if he is allowed to slip the field turning for home on a good-ground gallop, even moderate rivals tracking him (Pure Logic, Luminaries) will find it hard to reel him in.

Jafimgoso (Harry Skelton) will be navigating a congested midfield of redistributed hold-up horses; watch for him being blocked or carried wide at the top of the straight, which would critically compromise his finishing run.

Crafty Gael's 93-day absence and poor recent form (008) means Sean Bowen may find himself with little horse underneath him late in the race — if he is held up as normal and the pace is slow, he has no route into contention.

With four or more horses genuinely wanting to be held up and only one true front-runner, the early stages around Uttoxeter's tight bends could see interference and jostling for position — watch for Illico De Montave (329 days off) being caught in traffic on his comeback.

Pure Logic's trainer John Joseph Hanlon has had zero winners from 23 runners in the past 14 days — a cold stable stat — but the headgear (p) and prominent style at least gives Paddy Hanlon (5) a simple tactical brief of tracking Iamyouare throughout.

runners_data.name: Uhtred Ragnarson
runners_data.note: Alan King's five-year-old is a hold-up horse who handles good ground well — winning last time at 16f on good — and his recent course sim-going record (6 runs, 1 win, 5 places) marks him as credible if the race sets up for a late challenge; Tom Bellamy takes the ride.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner five starts back, Uhtred Ragnarson returns within 27 days, has run over today's going before, and rates a leading threat at 105; a fall in between remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Fiskardo
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's six-year-old is the race's lone front-runner with a solid record of placing in similar conditions, and his ability to dictate unchallenged gives him a clear tactical advantage; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) is not relevant here as leading is his natural role — the note is that he is racing in role, not out of it.
runners_data.comment: Placed in all of its last four starts, including a win three starts back, Fiskardo brings strong, consistent form into this and has run over today's going before, rating a leading threat at 105; a 45-day break is the only slight concern.

runners_data.name: October Hill
runners_data.note: David Pipe's six-year-old carries a tongue strap and hood and boasts a win at 20f on soft ground; his prominent style means he should travel just behind Fiskardo and is well-placed to strike if the leader weakens — nine sim-going runs without a win is a mild flag.
runners_data.comment: Brought down last time out having been a winner two starts back, and placed again three starts back, October Hill has run over today's trip and going before and rates a leading threat at 103; the unlucky exit last time is easily forgiven.

runners_data.name: Tommy Cullen
runners_data.note: A hold-up type with a consistent record of placing at this course and distance on good ground — four runs at 16f-21f on good, all mid-division finishes — Matt Crawley's eight-year-old offers staying ability but has not won since two outings ago and may need things to fall perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out after three consecutive fourths before that, Tommy Cullen still tops our figures at 114, clear of its 102 official mark, and remains the one to beat here despite being without a win in its last four starts.

runners_data.name: Sonyourastar
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's six-year-old is held up and has only two sim-going runs to assess, with no wins or places from those; form figures of 4,8,8,4 suggest he finds the line but lacks the class to threaten at these weights unless conditions become unusually testing.
runners_data.comment: A run of fourths and eighths without a win in its last five starts leaves Sonyourastar hard to fancy at 100 on our figures, though it has run over today's trip and going before and returns within a month of its last outing.

runners_data.name: The Secret Pearl
runners_data.note: Alex Hales trains this seven-year-old who is a genuine hold-up performer by nature — the midfield map position reflects overcrowding at the rear rather than her preferred racing style; a placed run at 16f on good ground is her best recent result and Kielan Woods will need space to deliver her late run.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a second five starts back, show she has ability, though modest finishes in between leave The Secret Pearl, still without a win in her last five starts, only a fair contender at 102, having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Ashdown Forest
runners_data.note: The freshest angle in the race — Dan Skelton's four-year-old won last time over 16f on good and Harry Skelton takes the ride, which is significant — but this horse holds up naturally and being shown in midfield reflects the crowded hold-up group rather than a change of tactics; the youth and fitness angle makes this the most interesting of the redistributed quartet.

runners_data.name: Papillondelumiere
runners_data.note: J R Barlow's eight-year-old is fitted with a tongue strap and a pully-pad and has gone 47 days since last running; three sim-going runs yield no wins or places, and the amateur rider claiming 7lb suggests limited expectations — this horse's natural hold-up style is squeezed further back than the map indicates.
runners_data.comment: A third four starts back is the highlight of a sparse profile, but a pulled-up run last time out and two modest finishes in between leave Papillondelumiere unexposed, without a win in its last four starts, and in need of more experience before fair judgment can be made.

runners_data.name: Mc'flo
runners_data.note: Anthony Carson's five-year-old has an all-good-ground profile but eight runs across 20f-23f without a win or place tells a clear story about limitations; genuinely a hold-up type who will be at the back of this compressed field in reality, and with Brendan Powell aboard the challenge looks considerable at these weights.
runners_data.comment: A run of finishes between fourth and ninth in its last five starts, without a win, leaves Mc'flo firmly among the outsiders on our figures at 77, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns within a month of her latest start.

races.paceDynamic: Fiskardo is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no rival willing or able to press him from the outset, he should secure an uncontested lead and control the tempo across the 2m4f trip on good ground at Uttoxeter. Behind him, October Hill is the most likely horse to track him prominently, while the remainder of the field — Uhtred Ragnarson, Tommy Cullen, Sonyourastar and the redistributed hold-up types — will be held up in a bunch. The field actually contains more genuine hold-up horses than the pace map can represent at the rear: The Secret Pearl, Ashdown Forest, Papillondelumiere and Mc'flo are all true hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield positions they are unlikely to secure naturally, meaning the chasing pack will be tightly compressed through the middle stages. With Fiskardo setting a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front, this race shape strongly favours a prominent racer or an athletic hold-up horse with a powerful staying finish — the clearest beneficiary of a steady-tempo, single-pace race will be whichever runner can travel fluently just off the pace and quicken when Fiskardo's advantage is challenged from two out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fiskardo Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Fiskardo leads from the start without pressure and dictates a controlled gallop, winning or finishing very close.
scenarios.body: Fiskardo sets his own rhythm with no rival willing to close him down early, conserving enough energy to build on his lead from two out; October Hill, tracking closest, has the best chance of running him down if he weakens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Overpowers Leader
scenarios.trigger: If October Hill or another prominent runner makes a decisive move at the second-last to overturn Fiskardo.
scenarios.body: October Hill has course form and travels well at a steady pace, giving him the platform to attack if Fiskardo's advantage narrows naturally entering the home straight; this shape rewards the horse sitting closest to the pace who can accelerate when the gaps open.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough to compress the field and a late finisher delivers a strong run from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: Uhtred Ragnarson or Tommy Cullen, both effective hold-up types on good ground, could pick up the pieces if the true hold-up runners are caught in traffic; Uhtred Ragnarson's recent course form on good ground makes him the most credible finisher from off the pace in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Defies Profile
scenarios.trigger: If one of the mapped-midfield hold-up horses — Ashdown Forest or The Secret Pearl — manages to secure a better position than expected and outstays rivals.
scenarios.body: Ashdown Forest, fresh off a recent win and trained by Dan Skelton, is the most likely to defy expectations if the pace compresses the field enough to bring a strong finisher into play; The Secret Pearl has placed form at this sort of trip on good ground but the style mismatch limits realistic expectations.

watchPoints.text: Fiskardo sets the entire race shape — if he jumps slowly or is taken on early by October Hill, the controlled tempo collapses and the hold-up horses gain a significant advantage.

Ashdown Forest raced just two days ago and while freshness can be an asset for Dan Skelton's horses, the extremely short turnaround at 4 years old over a longer trip than his hurdles win warrants monitoring in the market.

The cluster of true hold-up horses — The Secret Pearl, Papillondelumiere and Mc'flo — will likely create traffic problems turning for home if the pace compresses; watch for Kielan Woods on The Secret Pearl finding gaps late.

October Hill's headgear (tongue strap and hood) has featured across his recent runs including his win — consistency there is positive, but his sim-going record of 0 wins from 9 comparable runs is worth noting if he is short in the market.
Tommy Cullen has finished fourth four times in his last five runs — a pattern of consistent but unrewarded efforts that may continue if the pace does not fully collapse late.
